info.description:
# Introduction
DTN API for consuming mapping services

# Map Tile API Playground
A tool that can be used to easily view the layers you have access to using your obtained credentials. It also serves as a simple reference implementation of an interactive map viewer based on the Map Tile API.
Access the Map Tile API Playground [here](https://map.api.dtn.com/static/html/v2/map.html).

If you are migrating from V1 to V2 of the DTN Map Tile API, please refer to our [V2 Migration Guide](https://map.api.dtn.com/static/html/v2/migration_guide.pdf)
info.title: DTN Map Tile API

tags.name: Metadata
tags.description: Returns layer metadata such as zoom levels, bounding boxes, etc.

tags.name: Legends
tags.description: Returns layer legends in either html or image format.

tags.name: Styles
tags.description: Returns layer styles as defined by the MapBox Style Specification.

tags.name: Timestamps
tags.description: Returns each timestamp for each of the layers the system has tiles for.

tags.name: Tiles
tags.description:
Returns layer tiles in either raster or vector format. ## Token passing methods
Authorization header Token query parameter
Security More secure Less secure
Requires preflight OPTIONS request Yes No (more performant)
Ease of integration Requires manipulation of headers in the tile requests Does not require manipulation of headers in the tile request
When using the API from a browser, the recommended method is Token query parameter since it delivers higher throughput.

tags.name: Tooltips
tags.description: Returns tooltips in either application/json or text/html from a certain location. When using the API from a browser, the recommended method is Token query parameter since it delivers higher throughput.

tags.name: Tooltip templates
tags.description: Returns handlebar templates to be used for displaying tooltips.

tags.name: Geocoder
tags.description: Returns location information or geographic coordinates from a geocoding service. Supports forward and reverse geocoding.

tags.name: Image
tags.description: Allows generation of custom tailored map images

x-request-id.description: UUID compliant with RFC 4122 that uniquely identifies the request.

content-encoding.description: Lists any encodings that have been applied to the returned payload.

content-language.description: Describe the language(s) intended for the audience.

accept-json.name: Accept
accept-json.description: Indicates response media types that are acceptable.

accept-language.name: Accept-Language
accept-language.description:
Specifies the desired language and country code for language translation and formatting conventions.
Supported languages are English (en) and Spanish (es). However, any 2-letter ISO country code is supported as locale. See [here](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#search/code) for a list of country codes.
Defaults to English (en-US) if unsupported locale is specified.

accept-legend.name: Accept
accept-legend.description: Indicates response media types that are acceptable.

accept-tile.name: Accept
accept-tile.description: Indicates response media types that are acceptable.

accept-image.name: Accept
accept-image.description: Indicates response media types that are acceptable.

accept-tooltip.name: Accept
accept-tooltip.description: Indicates response media types that are acceptable.

accept-tooltip-template.name: Accept
accept-tooltip-template.description: Indicates response media types that are acceptable.

layer-id.name: layerId
layer-id.description: Unique identifier for the layer. See the full list of layers on the [DTN Map Tile Layer Catalog](https://map.api.dtn.com/static/html/v2/layer-catalog.html).

schema.description: id for the layer from which to receive data.

filter.name: filter
filter.description: Comma separated list of filter ids of a layer filter that the resulting data driven style would filter according to predefined filters.

schema.description: filter id for which the data driven style will include additional filter query

legend-title.name: legendTitle
legend-title.description: Indicates whether or not to include the layer name as a title in the legend.

max-width.name: maxWidth
max-width.description: max width of the legend image in pixels

tile-set-id.name: tileSetId
tile-set-id.description: tileSetId, as retrieved from the timestamps endpoint.

schema.description: id for the timestamp from which to receive data.

token.name: token
token.description: JSON Web Token in query parameter as an alternative to Authorization header.

tile-size.name: size
tile-size.description: It indicates the expected size for the tile. Only allowed for raster tiles

layer-parameters.name: parameters
layer-parameters.description: Key-value pair list, separated by semicolons, representing each of the desired parameter ids and values to  use against this endpoint. When available, parameters are defined in the metadata endpoint for each given layer.

time-range.name: time
time-range.description: Times range, in UTC and ISO 8601 compliant, delimited by a forward slash. The time range of data has a maximum of 24 hours allowed. This parameter is **optional**, and is mainly used for accessing older, archived data. If not given, returns the latest data available.

force-off-interval.name: forceOffInterval
force-off-interval.description: When set to true, this parameter forces the API to return the most recent time frame, even if it falls outside the regular intervals. If set to false or omitted, only data from the regular intervals is returned.

unit.name: unit
unit.description: Unit system (with or without industry specific overrides) to use when returning data.

timezone.name: timezone
timezone.description: A recognized geographical region in `Continent/Region` format that observes a uniform standard time. Follows the [IANA timezone database](https://data.iana.org/time-zones/tzdb-2021a/zone1970.tab).

enum: check the IANA database for more values

epsg.name: epsg
epsg.description:
Specifies the projection to be used, as defined by an EPSG code.
The EPSG code being used must be present in the supportedEPSGs metadata attribute for each of the layers requested.
When using a basemap style url, make sure to reference one using the same EPSG. Example values: - 3857 - Web Mercator - 3031 - Antarctic Polar Stereographic - 3995 - Arctic Polar Stereographic

locale.name: locale
locale.description:
Specifies the desired language and country code for language translation and formatting conventions.
Supported languages are English (en) and Spanish (es). However, any 2-letter ISO country code is supported as locale. See [here](https://www.iso.org/obp/ui/#search/code) for a list of country codes.
Defaults to English (en-US) if unsupported locale is specified.
If provided, overrides the Accept-Language header.

palette-override.name: paletteOverride
palette-override.description:
Value-color pair list separated by semicolons, denoting the custom color palette for the given layer.
Values may be a string or a number. When the value is a number, the decimal separator (if any) must be a "." (dot).
Colors may be hexadecimal color codes, or in RGB/RGBA notation. When using RGBA notation, the alpha value must be a float between 0 and 1.

smoothing-profile.name: smoothingProfile
smoothing-profile.description: The smoothing profile to use when rendering the layer. Defaults to `none` if not specified.

map-zoom.name: map-zoom
map-zoom.description: Zoom level used by the map viewer, this may or may not correspond to the tile being requested, which depends on tile size.

ext.name: ext
ext.description: File extension indicating format of choice.

schema.description: Data type returned, it overrides the Accept header when both are provided.

search-text.name: searchText
search-text.description: The location or place you are trying to look up. This could be an address, a point of interest name, a city name, etc.

lng-path.name: lng
lng-path.description: Longitude that specifies the location being queried.

lng.name: lng
lng.description: Longitude that specifies the location being queried.

lat-path.name: lat
lat-path.description: Latitude that specifies the location being queried.

lat.name: lat
lat.description: Latitude that specifies the location being queried.

will-persist.name: willPersist
will-persist.description: Specify whether to request persistent geocodes (`true`) or not (`false`, default). When persist is enabled, you are contractually allowed to temporarily cache or permanently store the response, and the backing geocoder service will charge these types of requests at a higher rate.

autocomplete.name: autocomplete
autocomplete.description: Specify whether to return autocomplete results (`true`) or not (`false`, default). When autocomplete is enabled, results will be included that start with the requested string, rather than just responses that match it exactly.

bbox.name: bbox
bbox.description: Limit results to only those contained within the supplied bounding box. Bounding boxes should be supplied as four numbers separated by commas, in minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat order. When bbox and country filters are both enabled, the request will utilize only the initial parameter specified.

country.name: country
country.description: Limit results to one or more countries. Permitted values are ISO 3166 alpha 2 country codes separated by commas. When bbox and country filters are both enabled, the request will utilize only the initial parameter specified.

limit.name: limit
limit.description: Specify the maximum number of results to return. The default is `5` and the maximum supported is `10`. This parameter is only relevant if the autocomplete feature is enabled. When autocomplete is disabled, the API will return a single result.

proximity.name: proximity
proximity.description: Bias the response to favor results that are closer to this location. Provided as two comma-separated coordinates in `longitude,latitude` order.

place_types.name: placeTypes
place_types.description: Filter results to include only a subset (one or more) of the available feature types. Options are `country`, `region`, `postcode`, `district`, `place`, `locality`, `neighborhood`, `address`. Multiple options can be comma-separated.

image-layers.name: layerIds
image-layers.description: Comma separated list of layer ids to render in stacking order.

image-opacities.name: opacities
image-opacities.description: Comma separated list of opacities to apply to each of the requested layers, in the same order as in the layerIds attribute. Layers with no matching opacity will use the default one being used in its style. Valid values from 0 to 1 inclusive.

image-smoothing-profiles.name: smoothingProfiles
image-smoothing-profiles.description: Comma separated list of smoothing profiles to apply to each of the requested layers, in the same order as in the layerIds attribute. Layers with no matching smoothing profile will not be smoothed.

image-timestamp.name: time
image-timestamp.description: Timestamp in UTC and ISO 8601 format. It indicates the time the image should be valid for.

schema.description: Timestamp for which the tile should be valid, defaults to current time

image-basemap-style-url.name: basemapStyleURL
image-basemap-style-url.description:
URL for a Mapbox data driven style defining a base map.
When using a custom one, please provide an access token. - Streets: mapbox://styles/dtn-mapbox/ckwv1d32r4vsw14poxf2forep - Dark: mapbox://styles/dtn-mapbox/ckwv21klw3k2v15pi0igs3uk1 - Light: mapbox://styles/dtn-mapbox/ckwv1z6fh5prn14pcdx8xqrja - Outdoors: mapbox://styles/dtn-mapbox/ckwv1rso35jf614mn4mc9fq82 - Satellite: mapbox://styles/dtn-mapbox/ckwv24fqs3k5e15pihmf9qtrc - Navigation-day: mapbox://styles/dtn-mapbox/ckwv2ch170bul14qg6xneqxri - Navigation-night: mapbox://styles/dtn-mapbox/ckwv2jjos05v215pcse1xqjw8 If using EPSG code of 3031 (Antarctic Polar Stereographic), the following styles must be use - 3031 Streets: https://map.api.dtn.com/static/layers/basemaps/3031/styles/street/style.json - 3031 Dark: https://map.api.dtn.com/static/layers/basemaps/3031/styles/dark/style.json - 3031 Light: https://map.api.dtn.com/static/layers/basemaps/3031/styles/light/style.json If using EPSG code of 3995 (Arctic Polar Stereographic), the following styles must be use - 3995 Streets: https://map.api.dtn.com/static/layers/basemaps/3995/styles/street/style.json - 3995 Dark: https://map.api.dtn.com/static/layers/basemaps/3995/styles/dark/style.json - 3995 Light: https://map.api.dtn.com/static/layers/basemaps/3995/styles/light/style.json

image-basemap-visibility-overrides.name: basemapVisibilityOverrides
image-basemap-visibility-overrides.description: Comma separated string of pairs like "layerId:true|false" defining layout visibility overrides for the basemap provided by the basemapStyleURL parameter. Wildcards are allowed in the layerId.

image-width.name: width
image-width.description: Width of the rendered image in pixels

image-height.name: height
image-height.description: Height of the rendered image in pixels

image-get-viewport.name: viewport
image-get-viewport.description:
Defines the area to be rendered using comma separated numbers. Area can be defined either through:
- lon,lat,zoom
lon should be between -180 and 180, lat between -90 and 90, zoom between 0 and 22 - minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat
minLon and maxLon should be between -360 and 360, minLat and maxLat between -90 and 90, zoom between 0 and 22, minLon < maxLon, minLat < maxLat

image-post-viewport.name: viewport
image-post-viewport.description:
Defines the area to be rendered using comma separated numbers. Area can be defined either through
- lon,lat,zoom
lon should be between -180 and 180, lat between -90 and 90, zoom between 0 and 22 - minLon,minLat,maxLon,maxLat
minLon and maxLon should be between -360 and 360, minLat and maxLat between -90 and 90, zoom between 0 and 22, minLon < maxLon, minLat < maxLat When doing POST with a style holding a geojson payload in the sources section, the viewport can be automatically adjusted to the incoming features, padding can be optionally added. - auto - auto,paddingInDegrees
paddingInDegrees should be between 0 and 10

clientCredentials.description:
# Using DAIS for M2M/API Auth
You have been given a Client ID and a Client Secret, which are used to request a DTN Access Token. DTN Access Tokens are required when making calls to each and every DTN API endpoint. The following information provides additional details on these tokens and how they are generated.
## What is an Access Token and how is it different from an API Key?
An API Key is a random string of characters that an API uses to authorize whether or not a calling client has approved access to an endpoint. These keys are a non-standard approach to API authorization and are generally issued on a per-API basis.

An Access Token is also a string of characters but is a base-64 encoded JavaScript Object Notation Web Token, or JWT. JWTs are a widely accepted standard that use OAuth concepts and approaches. 

Both API Keys and Access Tokens are used in an Authorization Request Header as a Bearer, meaning there is no difference in where you put this string of characters when you make calls to DTN APIs.
## How to generate an Access Token?
When requested, an Access Token is generated for your specific Client (ID/Secret) and for a specific API. The DTN Auth and Identity Service (DAIS) generates new Access Tokens for your client. The DAIS endpoint is `POST https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize`.

This endpoint takes two Header parameters:
  * `Content-Type: application/json`
  * `Accept: application/json`

This endpoint takes four parameters in the Request Body:
  * `grant_type`: this should always be client_credentials for generating machine-to-machine tokens.
  * `client_id`: this is the Client ID or Application ID using the token and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This ID will never change for your client/application.
  * `client_secret`: this is the Client Secret that is associated with the Application ID and is given to you by DTN's Identity Team. This key is subject to rotation for security purposes but always with the client's knowledge.
  * `audience`: this is the API for which this Access Token will be used. For the DTN Map Tile API, you need to use the following audience: https://map.api.dtn.com

You can use this CURL command template as a reference for obtaining an access token:
  ```
  curl --location --request POST 'https://api.auth.dtn.com/v1/tokens/authorize' \
--header 'Accept: application/json' \
--header 'Content-Type: application/json' \
--data-raw '{
"grant_type": "client_credentials",
"client_id": "insert your client id here",
"client_secret": "insert your client secret here",
"audience": "insert your audience here"
}' 
  ```

*This document, for demonstration purposes, supplies a client_id and client_secret in all code examples. This client/application is for a fictitious API and cannot be used in practice to gain unauthorized access to any other DTN API.*
Upon generating a new Access Token, you should receive an HTTP Response from DAIS similar to this:
  ```
  {
    "data": {
          "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InpfX21pZW13NGhoTmdvQWQxR3N6ciJ9..0VHdyp1w9PPFVI0FPheAwuKZwb5C25rwP-LPMXcSNoRmouvga1DZtNLA67ZzE_sAlc_VpaDRr6daLKr_Alw4347mw9sdjP8wKR27kCZa9JZK5PGQMmXHscATbzBEJYpCPklfyGaajgymqTBGnedcv8F0UvlRzQPsFeRPnVoX7BWOSXpMbyToGiXWkQLBQT7r96KAmLZOPJFZspPtjw-wH2mSL2WNa_nkB4j5vMGhGxlKiNRsKb30TH_WAel2hsxNlcPK3XHCmrMTYsNnu7HNqOTMn2i0__0rvBrhSWEw-_grqQDmWFJuWd7Qhi1q81AaJcdqgoSa_efz93QFclJUNw",
          "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
          "expires_in": 90,
          "token_type": "Bearer"
      },
      "meta": {
          "date_time": "2022-06-24T19:09:42.963Z",
          "name": "v1.tokens.authorize",
          "uuid": "ee6f9feb-dcf8-4421-a6fd-efd6beabdaa9",
          "start_timestamp": 1656097782509,
          "end_timestamp": 1656097782963,
          "execution_time": 454
      }
  }
  ```
Looking at this Response, you will see:
  * `access_token`: contains the JWT Access Token string you will use as your Bearer token.
  * `scope`: contains the scopes that this Access Token gives you permissions to access.
  * `expires_in`: contains the length of time before this Access Token will expire, in seconds.
  * `token_type`: verifies that this Access Token should be used as a Bearer token.

## How to use an Access Token after one is generated?
Once a new Access Token is obtained, it is used in each call to a DTN API endpoint as a Bearer token in an Authorization Request Header. For example:
  ```
  Header: 'Authorization: Bearer eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCIsImtpZCI6InpfX21pZW13NGhoTmdvQWQxR3N6ciJ9..0VHdyp1w9PPFVI0FPheAwuKZwb5C25rwP-LPMXcSNoRmouvga1DZtNLA67ZzE_sAlc_VpaDRr6daLKr_Alw4347mw9sdjP8wKR27kCZa9JZK5PGQMmXHscATbzBEJYpCPklfyGaajgymqTBGnedcv8F0UvlRzQPsFeRPnVoX7BWOSXpMbyToGiXWkQLBQT7r96KAmLZOPJFZspPtjw-wH2mSL2WNa_nkB4j5vMGhGxlKiNRsKb30TH_WAel2hsxNlcPK3XHCmrMTYsNnu7HNqOTMn2i0__0rvBrhSWEw-_grqQDmWFJuWd7Qhi1q81AaJcdqgoSa_efz93QFclJUNw'
  ```

## Deconstructing the Access Token
A DTN Access Token carries information within its JWT Body that is available on every API call. By deconstructing the JWT token, our Access Tokens will resemble:
  ```
  {
    "https://auth.dtn.com/customerId": "1234567890Demo",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/productCode": "DemoApiP",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp": "18.213.174.27",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/rps": "100",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/tier": "Basic",
    "https://auth.dtn.com/quota": "999999",
    "iss": "https://id.auth.dtn.com/",
    "sub": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM@clients",
    "aud": "https://demo-api.auth.dtn.com/",
    "iat": 1656099068,
    "exp": 1656099158,
    "azp": "nfyO3KiKPR8N0DKR5CL8jS9GFBCDeyFM",
    "scope": "read:demo create:demo update:demo",
    "gty": "client-credentials",
    "permissions": [
      "read:demo",
      "create:demo",
      "update:demo"
    ]
  }
  ```
### Description of Claims

  | Claim                              | Type                                        | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
  | -----------------------------------| --------------------------------------------| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/customerId`  | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Customer ID found in the DTN Order Management/Salesforce system associated with this token.                                                                                                |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/productCode` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the Identity product code associated with this token.                                                                                                                                          |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/requesterIp` | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the IP address of the requesting client.                                                                                                                                                       |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/rps`         | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum rate per second this customer is authorized to utilize.                                                                                                                            |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/tier`        | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the data tier the customer purchased for the requested access.                                                                                                                                 |
  | `https://auth.dtn.com/quota`       | String                                      | Custom DTN claim containing the maximum yearly quota the customer purchased for calling DTN endpoints for the specific product.                                                                                            |
  | `iss`                              | String (URI)                                | The Security Token Service (STS) that issues and returns the token. If this value is not from `https://id.auth.dtn.com/`, the token should not be considered trusted.                                                      |
  | `sub`                              | String (URI)                                | The principle about which the token asserts information (the User ID or Client ID within the Identity Provider). A User ID will start with a prefix of `auth0\|`, while the Client ID will end with the suffix `@clients`. |
  | `aud`                              | String \| Array (Strings) (URI \| [URI, …]) | Identifies the intended recipient(s) of the token – its audience. The token should be rejected if the audience does not contain values expected by the calling application.                                                |
  | `iat`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | “Issued At” indicates when the authentication for this token occurred.                                                                                                                                                     |
  | `exp`                              | Number (Timestamp)                          | The “expiration time” on or after which the JWT must not be accepted for processing.                                                                                                                                       |
  | `azp`                              | String                                      | The application/client ID of the client using the token. The application can cat as itself or on behalf of a user.                                                                                                         |
  | `gty`                              | String (Space-delimited)                    | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |
  | `permissions`                      | Array (Strings)                             | The grant type that was used to request the token – not an RFC 7519 registered claim (Auth0-specific).                                                                                                                     |

detail.description: A human-readable description of the specific error.

type.description: A URL to a document describing the error condition.

title.description: A short, human-readable title for the general error type.

instance.description: URL with the id for the specific error; this will often point to an error log for that specific response.

parent.description: Reference to a parent group, null indicates root level.

hexColor.description: Hexadecimal color defined by 8 (hex triplet + alpha) characters.

overlays.description: List of overlays to render, it can be a mix of DTN layers and other custom MapBox data driven styles

opacity.description: Applies to DTN layers, controls its opacity, will be ignored if the style property is defined

tileSetId.description: Applies to all DTN layers. It has to match a tileSetId returned by the timestamp endpoint. It indicates the moment in time the layerId is valid for

filters.description: Applies to DTN layers for which there are filters defined. Will be ignored if the style property is defined

oneOf.description: Mapbox data driven style. Allows to provide custom overlays or override the default style for a given DTN layer
URL for a mapbox data driven style

insertBeforeLayerId.description: Layer ID associated with either the specified base map or with another layer ID in the overlay list which determines the placement of the overlay. Allows the integration of weather layers with the base map or the reorganization of overlays on the map.

visibilityOverrides.description: Applies to either DTN layers or custom style defined in the overlay. It allows to override the layout visibility property for the data driven style by indicating pairs of settings like "layerId:true|false:" to modify visibility of selected layers. Wildcards can be used in the layerId.

paletteOverride.description:
Value-color pair list separated by semicolons, denoting the custom color palette for the given layer.
Values may be a string or a number. When the value is a number, the decimal separator (if any) must be a "." (dot).
Colors may be hexadecimal color codes, or in RGB/RGBA notation. When using RGBA notation, the alpha value must be a float between 0 and 1.

smoothingProfile.description:
The smoothing profile to use when rendering the layer.
Available values are none, low, medium, high. Defaults to `none` if not specified.

unit.description: When available, units used in each of the values in the colorTable.

colorTableType.description: Indicates the type of elements in the color table, describing ranges, discrete values or categories.

colorTable.description: List of items of the type specified by colorTableType. Elements define the colors used for each possible value in the tile.

category.description: Text value to map against a color.

value.description: Numeric value to map against a color. When used in a range, this indicates the lower boundary of a range. When it is not present, it covers all possible values before/after the adjacent item of the list.

maxZoom.description: Highest zoom level available for the given layer.

minZoom.description: Lowest zoom level available for the given layer.

label.description: Layer label, a text in between the id and the description.

numArchiveDays.description: Number of archive days configured for the layer. Null for static layers.

oldestDataAvailable.description: Timestamp for the oldest data available for the layer in ISO 8601, in UTC. Null when not available.

dataType.description: Indicates whether the layer delivers observations, forecasts, or a static tile set.

supportedEPSGs.description:
Supported EPSG codes to be used against the static image API.
Example values:
  - 3857 - Web Mercator
  - 3031 - Antarctic Polar Stereographic
  - 3995 - Arctic Polar Stereographic

formatsAvailable.description:
Indicates the different media types available in the tiles endpoint, either through the Accept header or file extension. Example values with their corresponding extension:
Accept header File extension
image/png png
image/webp webp
